players.product: 800G/1.6T optical transceivers + high-power ELSFP lasers (US-anchored manufacturing)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2025 HEADLINE RESULTS: record revenue of $134,300,000, +34% year over year and +13% sequentially, in line with the $125,000,000 to $140,000,000 guidance; non-GAAP gross margin 31.4% (above the 29% to 31% guide, up from 31% in Q3 2025 and 28.9% a year ago, on favorable mix and cost reduction); non-GAAP loss per share $0.01 vs a guided loss of $0.13 to $0.04; non-GAAP operating loss $7,100,000; GAAP net loss $2,000,000. Revenue mix: 56% data center, 40% CATV, 4% FTTH/telecom/other. Full-year 2025 revenue rose 83% to a record $456,000,000 with CATV revenue nearly tripling to $245,000,000. Revenue is net of warrant contra revenue (approximately 2.5% of revenue from warrant-holding customers; $730,000 in Q4).

DATA CENTER SPEED MIX: Q4 data center revenue $74,900,000, up 69% year over year and 70% sequentially. 100G sales +54% Y/Y and 400G sales +141% Y/Y. Data center revenue split: 51% 100G, 41% 200G/400G, 8% 10G/40G. 800G revenue came in below the $4,000,000 to $8,000,000 expectation because of ongoing firmware optimization at the hyperscale customer - CFO Stefan Murry said it was 'a bit below $4,000,000' - but strength in 400G with that customer more than offset it. Q1 data center growth expected to come principally from continued 400G growth plus some 800G.

800G RAMP TIMING: during Q4 AOI received an 800G volume order from one of its major hyperscale customers after that customer qualified AOI's 800G products (the CFO called it the 'first 800G volume order'; the CEO's turn as printed says 'fourth'). The remaining hurdle is firmware interoperability across the customer's many switch platforms ('Hardware-wise, everything is fine'), agreed to be finished around mid-March; AOI had expected a green light to ship in December. Production is already ramping for a strong 800G volume ramp starting in Q2 FY2026, when 800G is expected to be the largest data center product line at 'more than $25,000,000' (CEO: customer demand could be '$35,000,000 to $40,000,000'), gated by capacity not demand. Taiwan was qualified for several 800G product types in 2025; Texas is qualified for some 800G products with full qualification expected by mid-year. 800G and 1.6T run on the same automated lines with different final test; 1.6T expected to begin contributing to revenue later in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 800G Q2 FY2026 revenue more than $25,000,000; demand $35,000,000 to $40,000,000; firmware fix around March; Texas full qualification by mid-year

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY PLAN (early-2026 version, later raised): AOI exited 2025 with approximately 90,000 units per month of 800G capacity (near its 100,000 units per month target), roughly 31% of it in the U.S. It signed a lease for an additional Sugar Land, Texas building and began construction 'earlier this month' (per the February 26, 2026 call). Target: over 500,000 pieces of 800G and 1.6 terabit products per month by the end of 2026, about a quarter of that output from Texas. CEO Thompson Lin: by the end of 2027 more than 55% would be manufactured in the U.S. ('or even 60% or 65% for 1.6T'), and 'more than 80% to 85% of investment will be in Texas'; U.S. expansion is slower because of cleanroom build, equipment, qualification and training. Management says 800G demand is projected to exceed its production capacity through mid-2027.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 90,000 units per month of 800G at YE2025 (roughly 31% US); over 500,000 pieces per month of 800G+1.6T by end-2026 (about a quarter from Texas); more than 55% US by end-2027

quarterly_data.signal: MID-2027 RUN-RATE TARGET (first version; the Q2 FY2026 call later raised the 1.6T piece): by mid-2027 management expects 100G and 400G revenue of approximately $90,000,000 monthly, 800G approximately $217,000,000 monthly and 1.6 terabit approximately $71,000,000 monthly - $378,000,000 in monthly transceiver revenue in total (CFO clarified this is Q2 2027, 'not this year'), limited by capacity and supply chain rather than demand. CEO: with the 1.6T portion (whose gross margin is 'much, much higher'), overall transceiver gross margin should be 35% to 38% by Q2 2027, and more than 40% for all transceivers by Q4 2027; the long-term company objective is non-GAAP gross margin around 40%.
quarterly_data.figure: mid-2027: 100G+400G approximately $90,000,000 monthly, 800G approximately $217,000,000 monthly, 1.6T approximately $71,000,000 monthly = $378,000,000 monthly; transceiver GM 35% to 38% by Q2 2027, more than 40% by Q4 2027

quarterly_data.signal: GUIDANCE: Q1 FY2026 revenue $150,000,000 to $165,000,000 (sequential growth in both CATV and data center), non-GAAP gross margin 29% to 31% (400G mix headwind offset by expanding CATV margins), non-GAAP net income a loss of $7,000,000 to a loss of $300,000, non-GAAP EPS a loss of $0.09 to breakeven on approximately 76,400,000 shares; CATV Q1 revenue $61,000,000 to $67,000,000. Full-year 2026: over $1,000,000,000 in revenue with non-GAAP operating profit of over $120,000,000 - a level 'limited by our production capacity and supply chain, not market demand' (CEO: 'minimum 99% confident'). Sustainable non-GAAP profitability expected beginning Q2 2026; strong sequential growth in H1 with acceleration in H2 as capacity comes online. 2026 capex projections to be shared later.

ORDER PIPELINE AND CUSTOMER BASE: the CEO said AOI has 'almost two years of loading forecast from more than one customer' for 800G, that at least two or even three customers 'would like to buy all the transceiver we can make for 800G and 1.6', and that within less than three months AOI should receive more than $100,000,000 of 800G transceiver orders and more than $200,000,000 of 1.6T transceiver orders (customers may sign agreements to lock in AOI's commitments). Another existing hyperscale customer indicated it intends to order 800G soon and wants to qualify AOI's 1.6T; a new hyperscale customer began discussing qualification of 800G and 1.6T. Q4 concentration: top 10 customers 96% of revenue; three greater-than-10% customers - one CATV at 39% and two data center at 31% and 21%, one of which is a U.S.-based large hyperscale customer that became a 10% customer 'for the first time in a long time'. For 2026 the CFO sees the roughly $700,000,000 of non-CATV revenue dominated by two roughly equivalent hyperscale customers plus a smaller third; the CEO expects three hyperscale customers above 10%.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $100,000,000 of 800G orders and more than $200,000,000 of 1.6T orders expected within three months; Q4 customers 39% / 31% / 21%; top 10 = 96%

quarterly_data.signal: IN-HOUSE LASERS AND THE LASER SHORTAGE: the CEO said there is 'a huge issue of laser shortage' and (as transcribed) 'even some supplier to us want to get this from them'; by the end of 2026 'more than 95% of laser will be AI laser'. AOI announced a $300,000,000 Texas investment to more than triple its indium phosphide laser manufacturing by mid-2027, with line of sight to all the equipment needed. CFO: in-house lasers let AOI avoid shortages affecting others, and CPO will continue to drive increased demand for high-power lasers, so laser capacity in Texas will keep expanding. In 800G and 1.6T designs less than 10% of component value is sourced from China, with a path to near zero.
quarterly_data.figure: $300,000,000 Texas investment; laser capacity more than triple by mid-2027; more than 95% AI lasers by end-2026; less than 10% China-sourced component value

quarterly_data.signal: CAPEX, BALANCE SHEET AND TARIFFS: Q4 capital investments of $84,000,000, mainly for 400G and 800G capacity; full-year 2025 capital investments of $209,000,000, above the $120,000,000 to $150,000,000 projection given a year earlier, due to increased customer demand projections. Cash, equivalents, short-term investments and restricted cash $216,000,000 (vs $150,700,000 at end of Q3); debt excluding convertibles $67,300,000; inventory $183,100,000 (vs $170,200,000), mainly raw materials for rising production. Direct tariffs cost $1,200,000 on the income statement and $3,100,000 on capital equipment in Q4; AOI was importer of record for 'many, if not most' of its 2025 tariff shipments and is evaluating recovery of IEEPA tariffs after the court decision.

CATV (non-AI segment): Q4 CATV revenue $54,000,000, up 3% Y/Y and down 24% sequentially from a record Q3, in line with the $50,000,000 to $55,000,000 expectation; significant 1.8 GHz amplifier shipments to its largest CATV customer continued, plus momentum with a newer set of MSO customers (none as large as the largest). Management still believes nearly $300,000,000 of annual CATV revenue is feasible, mostly amplifiers with some Quantum Link software revenue in 2026. Telecom revenue $5,100,000, +45% Y/Y.
quarterly_data.figure: CATV rev $54,000,000 (+3% Y/Y, -24% Q/Q); nearly $300,000,000 annual CATV potential
